claims.text: Adding Si to CrFeCoNi promotes formation of a mixed chromium–Si oxide scale.
Adding Al to CrFeCoNi promotes formation of a mixed chromium–Al oxide scale.
The mixed chromium–X oxide has improved lattice coherence and reduced thermal strain.
Using Mn as X predominantly produces less compatible, defective oxides.
Stable, coherent protective scales form only when X enables a secondary oxide phase that bonds well with Cr2O3.
For X = Si or Al, a silicate or alumina secondary oxide nucleates and is thermodynamically compatible with Cr2O3.
The mixed oxide system reduces lattice mismatch at the metal–oxide interface.
The mixed oxide system reduces thermal-expansion differences at the metal–oxide interface.
Reduced lattice mismatch and thermal-expansion differences minimize interfacial stress and prevent oxide cracking or spallation.
For X = Mn, spinels or less-adherent manganese oxides fail to provide the proposed stress-relief effect.
Mn-containing scales become unstable, cracked, or spalled because of poor phase compatibility.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will form continuous, coherent, adherent oxide scales that persist during high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn will form oxide scales that crack or spall because of poor phase compatibility and higher interfacial stresses.
The proposed comparison uses CrFeCoNi without a beneficial secondary-phase-forming element, or CrFeCoNiMn, as the baseline under matched exposure conditions.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Single- versus multiphase alloy microstructures may alter oxide-scale formation behavior.
The magnitude of the proposed benefit may depend on composition, processing route, and environmental factors.
A controlled test is proposed at 950 °C for 100 hours using CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Si, Mn, and Al while holding other compositional factors constant.
Failure of Si- or Al-containing alloys to show greater oxide-scale coherence and adhesion than the Mn-containing alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
